## Critique
- claim-1: Correctly grounded as a theorem statement over \(\mathbb Z\), but minimal generation alone does not imply an integral basis of indecomposables.
- claim-2: The no-syzygy statement is source-backed, but its large-\(N\) proof uses the invalid general principle that specializing variables in an inconsistent system preserves inconsistency [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 790-825].
- claim-3: The conditional argument is correct. Homogeneous generation converts a kernel element in \(J_v/A_+J_v\) into the prohibited syzygy; injectivity of the free residue map excludes torsion. Schur weight is preserved, with ordinary cohomological degree doubled.
- claim-4: This is the decisive missing certificate. It is repaired below.
- claim-5: Correct. Lemma 4.3 controls only embedded rows, not all enlarged equations [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 777-818].
- claim-6: Passes audit after the lower theorem is repaired. Conjugation sends \(q^r\) to \(r^q\), \(i^j\) to \(j^i\), preserves Schur weight and integral coefficients, and maps \(A_+\) onto \(A^\vee_+\). The displayed transformed parameters satisfy all bigrassmannian inequalities and give \((i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b)\).
- claim-7: Passes audit. The conjugate-shape formula is exact, and nilpotence of \(A_+\) in the finite graded Grassmannian quotient makes the graded Nakayama argument valid.

## Repair certificates
- [proof-attempt] Let \(q=n-r\), \(C=(q-i)^j\), and let \(P\) kill every enlarged variable except \(A_{\lambda,\theta}\) with \(\lambda\subseteq b^a\) and \(\theta\subseteq C\). For a wide \(\tau\in\operatorname{Dec}_{\widehat\varphi}\), write
  \[
  B=\tau_B\subseteq b^a,\qquad
  R=\tau_R=(\tau_1-i,\ldots,\tau_{\widehat j}-i),
  \]
  deleting trailing zeroes. Then \(R\ne\varnothing\) and \(|B|+|R|=N\).

  If \(R\subseteq C\), define
  \[
  \nu=(i+R_1,\ldots,i+R_j,B_1,\ldots,B_a),
  \]
  with zero padding. Since \(R_1\le q-i\), \(\ell(R)\le j\), \(B_1\le b\le i\), and \(j+a\le r\), this is a wide member of \(\operatorname{Dec}_\varphi\), and \(\tau=\widehat\nu\). Lemma 4.3 therefore gives
  \[
  P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau))
  =\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu).
  \]

  If \(R\nsubseteq C\), Proposition 3.3’s wide-row formula expresses every retained coefficient as
  \[
  \sum_\mu c_{\lambda,\mu}^{B}c_{\mu,R}^{\theta},
  \qquad \theta\subseteq C.
  \]
  A nonzero \(c_{\mu,R}^{\theta}\) requires \(R\subseteq\theta\), impossible because \(\theta\subseteq C\) while \(R\nsubseteq C\). Hence
  \[
  P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau))=0.
  \]
  Thus every enlarged wide row projects either to an original wide row or to zero:
  \[
  P(\operatorname{Lin}_{\widehat\varphi}(\tau))
  \in
  \operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}
  \{\operatorname{Lin}_\varphi(\nu):
  \nu\in\operatorname{Dec}_\varphi\text{ wide}\}.
  \]
  There are no additional tall rows: \(R=\varnothing\) and \(B\subseteq b^a\) uniquely give the embedded original tall row. Consequently any solution of the original system, extended by zero on discarded variables, would solve every enlarged equation, contradicting enlarged inconsistency. This repairs the large-\(N\) descent.

## Required revisions
- Replace the unsupported specialization assertion at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 817-818] with the certificate above.
- **Requested target established:** after this repair, the lower-adjoined integral-basis theorem follows, and the audited quotient-conjugation isomorphism and right-adjoined theorem follow integrally, grading-preservingly, and without torsion.
